title: Java Streams API Lazy Pipeline & Optional
subtitle: Master the functional Streams API, lazy intermediate operations, pull-based terminal evaluation with vertical loop fusion, short-circuiting, and NPE-free Optional chaining.
mentalModel: A Stream is not a data structure; it is a pipeline of computational descriptions. Intermediate steps are lazy; terminal operations pull data vertically one element at a time; Optional provides a monadic wrapper for nullable returns.

failureModes: Stream Re-use Exception: Attempting to invoke a terminal operation on an already consumed stream throws `IllegalStateException: stream has already been operated upon or closed`.
Using Optional as Method Parameters or Fields: Optional is not Serializable and incurs object allocation overhead; it is designed strictly as a return type for methods that may return no result.
tradeOffs: Streams vs Traditional For-Loops: Streams provide declarative readability, easy parallelism (`parallelStream()`), and vertical fusion, but may introduce minor lambda boxing/unboxing overhead for simple primitive iterations.
theoryData.productionScenario: In e-commerce microservices, refactoring nested iterative discount calculations into a stream pipeline with `parallelStream()` and `Collectors.groupingByConcurrent()` achieved a 3.8x throughput increase on multi-core AWS EC2 instances.

interviewQA.q: What is Vertical Loop Fusion in Java Streams?
interviewQA.a: Instead of executing each pipeline operation (e.g. filter) horizontally across the entire dataset into intermediate buffers, Java Streams fuse operations vertically. A single element passes through filter, map, and collect before the next element is pulled, optimizing CPU L1 cache locality.

interviewQA.q: What is the difference between `Optional.orElse()` and `Optional.orElseGet()`?
interviewQA.a: `orElse(expensiveMethod())` always executes `expensiveMethod()` regardless of whether the Optional contains a value or not. `orElseGet(() -> expensiveMethod())` is lazy and executes the Supplier only when the Optional is empty.

quizData.question: Do intermediate operations like `.filter()` or `.map()` execute when called without a terminal operation?
quizData.answer: No! Intermediate operations are strictly lazy. No computation occurs until a terminal operation (like .collect(), .count(), .reduce()) is triggered.

quizData.question: Can a single Stream instance be operated on twice by invoking two terminal operations?
quizData.answer: No! A Stream is a single-use pipeline. Attempting to consume it a second time throws an IllegalStateException.
